title: EventPulse · Load Test Truth
description: Reusable, parameterized load-test dashboard: verdict, k6 validity, client vs server, Node runtime, machine/kernel, overlays, post-run knee analysis. One dashboard for every stage: select run, role, service and host with variables.

list.name: route
list.label: Route (k6)
list.description: k6 route slug, e.g. health, cpu-n-25, echo-1024b

list.name: testid
list.label: Run (testid)
list.description: One k6 run. All = every run in the time range.

list.name: role
list.label: Role
list.description: victim = route under test; antagonist = background load; stall = one-shot blocker. All matches every role.

list.name: service
list.label: Service
list.description: Services exposing Node runtime metrics (default label service).

list.name: server_cpus
list.label: Server CPUs
list.description: Regex of CPU ids the server is pinned to (taskset), e.g. 0|6

list.name: k6_cpus
list.label: k6 CPUs
list.description: Regex of CPU ids k6 is pinned to

list.name: spare_cpus
list.label: Spare CPUs
list.description: Regex of CPU ids left idle

options.content:
**Pick a run:** `testid` (and optionally `script` / `route` / `role`). **Verdict first, then evidence.**
Read top to bottom: **0** is the run valid and what is the headline? · **1** did k6 tell the truth? · **2** client vs server (where did the time go?) · **3** the service process · **4** machine and kernel · **5** overlays that prove *what saturated* · **6** post-run comparison (expand after a series).

**A run is only trustworthy if:** *Generator headroom* = OK (no dropped iterations, unless it is a stall test) · generator cores < 70% · VUs not exhausted.
**Role filter:** `victim` is the route under test; `antagonist` is background load; `stall` is the one-shot blocker. Latency panels default to `victim`.
**Tags in play:** testid, rate, series, route, script (runner) · role, scenario, name, status (k6) · service, instance, route, status_code (server).

panels.title: 0 · Verdict (peak over the selected time range)
Generator headroom
panels.description: OK = k6 started every request on schedule (0 dropped iterations). DROPPED = the load generator was the bottleneck: discard the run (expected only in stall tests, where k6 cannot queue).

panels.title: Dropped % of offered
panels.description: dropped / (dropped + sent) over the range.

panels.title: Peak offered rps
panels.description: What the schedule asked for: achieved + dropped.

panels.title: Peak achieved rps
panels.description: Completed requests per second as seen by k6.

panels.title: Generator hottest core
panels.description: Busiest k6 core (K6_CPUS). Keep under 70%: above that the generator distorts latency.

panels.title: VU saturation
panels.description: k6 active VUs / max VUs. Near 100% means the next slow response causes dropped iterations.

panels.title: Peak p99 (k6, role)
panels.description: Client-side p99 from the native histogram, filtered by role.

panels.title: Peak p99.9 (k6, role)
panels.description: Tail: the number averages hide.

panels.title: Peak error %
panels.description: Failed requests (non-2xx/3xx, timeouts) as a fraction of requests.

panels.title: Peak loop lag excess p99
panels.description: p99 event-loop lag minus the 10 ms sampling floor of prom-client. >0 means requests wait behind JS.

panels.title: Hottest server core
panels.description: Busiest core in SERVER_CPUS. A single-threaded Node process saturates one core at ~100%.

panels.title: ListenOverflows (total)
panels.description: Connections dropped because the accept queue was full. Any non-zero value is saturation evidence.

panels.title: 1 · Did the test tell the truth? (k6, client side)
Offered vs achieved
panels.description: Offered = achieved + dropped. A gap means k6 (not the server) failed to keep schedule. Past the knee, achieved flattens while offered keeps rising.

panels.title: Dropped iterations /s
panels.description: k6 could not start these requests on schedule (no free VU). Zero is the validity condition.

panels.title: VUs active vs max
panels.description: If active hits max, the open model degrades into drops.

panels.title: Latency percentiles (k6 native histogram, log axis)
panels.description: True per-window percentiles: histogram_quantile(rate()). Needs k6 TREND_AS_NATIVE_HISTOGRAM=true and Prometheus --enable-feature=native-histograms. Filtered by $role. Dashed line = 50 ms.

panels.title: p99 by role (victim vs antagonist vs stall)
panels.description: Interference experiments: the victim's p99 next to the background route's. Ignores the $role filter on purpose.

panels.title: Responses by status
panels.description: Rate by HTTP status as seen by k6. 4xx/5xx show up here the moment protection (429/503) starts.

panels.title: Error rate (k6)
panels.description: Fraction of failed requests (non-2xx/3xx, timeouts, resets).

panels.title: Bandwidth (k6 sent / received)
panels.description: Bytes on the wire as k6 sees them. Payload-size experiments become bandwidth-bound here.

panels.title: 2 · Client vs server: where did the time go? (k6 + service metrics)
Client p99 vs server p99 / p50
panels.description: Client p99 minus server p99 is time spent OUTSIDE the handler: accept queue, event-loop backlog, network, generator. A growing gap is queueing.

panels.title: Time outside the handler (client p99 − server p99)
panels.description: The queueing signal. ~0 is healthy; it rises sharply at the knee because requests wait before the handler even runs.

panels.title: Throughput: client sent vs server handled
panels.description: Should overlap. If k6 sent more than the server handled, requests are failing, timing out or still in flight.

panels.title: Server requests by route
panels.description: RED: rate per route (excludes /metrics and /debug/stats).

panels.title: Server responses by status code
panels.description: RED: errors. 4xx/5xx from the service itself.

panels.title: Little's Law: in-flight vs rate × latency
panels.description: Expected concurrency L = λ·W = sum(rate(duration_sum)). Actual in-flight above expected = time spent before/around the handler (event-loop backlog, accept queue) = saturation.

panels.title: Server latency distribution (heatmap)
panels.description: Distribution shape over time from the classic histogram buckets. Bimodal bands reveal GC pauses, stalls, or one slow route hiding behind a good p50.

panels.title: 3 · What is the service process doing? (Node runtime, prom-client)
Event loop lag (log axis)
panels.description: p50/p99/max of event-loop delay (10 ms sampling resolution, so ~10 ms is the idle floor).

panels.title: Event loop lag excess (minus 10 ms floor)
panels.description: Zero until the loop is genuinely busy; the cleanest saturation signal for a single-threaded server.

panels.title: Process CPU (1.0 = one full core)
panels.description: User vs system CPU of the service. A single-threaded Node process tops out near 1.0 (plus GC and worker threads).

panels.title: CPU cost per request (µs)
panels.description: Total and kernel (system) CPU per handled request. The efficiency curve: flat then rising near saturation. Only shown above 100 rps.

panels.title: GC time (fraction of wall time)
panels.description: Share of time spent in GC by kind. Spikes line up with p99/p99.9 outliers.

panels.title: Heap / RSS / external memory
panels.description: Leaks show as a steady upward trend across a soak.

panels.title: File descriptors
panels.description: Open vs max FDs of the service. EMFILE starts at the limit.

panels.title: Active handles / resources
panels.description: Libuv handles (sockets, timers) and total active resources held by the process. Growth under constant load means a leak.

panels.title: Worker pool (busy / queue)
panels.description: Worker threads computing and jobs waiting. A growing queue = demand above worker capacity (E0.4).

panels.title: /echo body size (p50 / p99)
panels.description: Request payload sizes seen by the service (E0.9 payload sweep).

panels.title: 4 · Is the machine or the kernel the limit? (node_exporter)
Per-CPU utilisation
panels.description: One line per core. A pinned single-threaded server shows one core pinned at ~100% while the rest idle.

panels.title: CPU groups: server vs k6 vs spare
panels.description: Pinning check. Server cores should be hot, k6 cores below 70%, spare cores idle. If not, pinning (taskset) or CPU lists are wrong.

panels.title: CPU by mode (whole machine, stacked)
panels.description: user / system / softirq (network stack) / iowait / steal. Steal means a noisy neighbour on shared cloud CPUs: do not trust the run.

panels.title: Run queue vs cores
panels.description: Runnable processes versus core count. Sustained runnable > cores means CPU contention.

panels.title: Context switches /s
panels.description: Voluntary + involuntary switches. Spikes under oversubscription (too many runnable threads).

panels.title: TCP retransmits
panels.description: Segment and SYN retransmits. Loopback should be ~0; rises mean loss or an overflowing queue.

panels.title: Accept queue drops
panels.description: ListenOverflows / ListenDrops: the kernel dropped connections because the server did not accept() fast enough. Direct proof of saturation.

panels.title: TCP sockets vs ephemeral-port ceiling
panels.description: TIME_WAIT and in-use sockets against the ephemeral port range ($ephemeral_ports). Approaching the line = port exhaustion without keep-alive (E0.6).

panels.title: Listen queue length (textfile exporter)
panels.description: Recv-Q / Send-Q of the listening socket, from the listen-queue exporter. Recv-Q growing means the accept queue is filling.

panels.title: Loopback traffic
panels.description: Bytes/s over lo. Large payload tests saturate memory copy long before a NIC.

panels.title: Network (non-loopback): bytes and packets
panels.description: Cloud NICs have bandwidth AND packets-per-second ceilings; small events hit PPS first. Keep this ready for Stage 8.

panels.title: Throughput vs CPU saturation
panels.description: Left: achieved rps. Right: hottest server core and hottest generator core. The knee is where rps stops following the offered rate while a server core pins at ~100% and the generator stays below 70%.

panels.title: Latency vs queueing signals
panels.description: p99 and loop-lag excess (left, seconds, log) with accept-queue overflows (right). p99 bends, lag excess appears, overflows start: three signals agreeing is proof, one is a hint.

panels.title: Run comparison: achieved rps per testid
panels.description: One line per selected run. Compare runs of the same route (3 repeats) or different routes.

panels.title: Run comparison: p99 per testid
panels.description: Same runs, client p99.

panels.title: 6 · Post-run analysis (collapsed on purpose: expand AFTER a series, with the time range covering all runs)
Per-run summary (one row per testid)
panels.description: Set the time range to cover the whole series, then read down: achieved rps, drops, latency and errors per run. Role-filtered.

targets.expr: 100 * (sum by (testid) (increase(k6_dropped_iterations_total{testid=~"$testid",role=~"$role"}[$__range])) or (sum by (testid) (increase(k6_http_reqs_total{testid=~"$testid",role=~"$role"}[$__range])) * 0)) / ((sum by (testid) (increase(k6_dropped_iterations_total{testid=~"$testid",role=~"$role"}[$__range])) or (sum by (testid) (increase(k6_http_reqs_total{testid=~"$testid",role=~"$role"}[$__range])) * 0)) + sum by (testid) (increase(k6_http_reqs_total{testid=~"$testid",role=~"$role"}[$__range])))

panels.title: Knee curve: peak achieved rps (X) vs p99 (Y), one dot per run
panels.description: Dots move right while latency is flat, then shoot up at the knee. Quote capacity at ~70% of the knee rps. If axes look wrong, edit and choose X = Achieved peak rps, Y = p99.
